Hi team — I ran the 48h sample through our sizing model and sketched a validation plan. Key points summarized below. Spreadsheet attached.

Sizing recommendation (baseline):
- Model profile: open-llm-compatible 7B-class quantized runtime (q8_0) with KV cache enabled; fallback plan for int8 if latency regresses.
- Node mix: 4 x high-throughput nodes (A100-80GB equiv) + 8 x standard-quant nodes (cost-optimized) for a starting pool. This gives ~520 concurrent capacity headroom with autoscale buffers.
- Expected p95 under staging replay: 160–200ms if KV warm and batching thresholds set to 20ms.

Validation/acceptance plan (detailed):
1) Staging replay (72h): live traffic replay to staging fleet mirrors; success criteria: p95 <= 220ms, error rate < 0.2%, sustained throughput target within 10% of observed production peaks.
2) Pre-swap smoke (2 hours): Canary route 5% traffic to green, run canonical test suite (end-to-end prompts + function-calling checks).
3) Swap weekend: rolling cutover using blue/green with incremental ramp to 50% (2h), 75% (2h), 100% gateway switch.
4) Rollback plan: gateway revert to blue, disable new routing, invalidate caches if we detect p95 > 300ms or sustained error spikes > 0.5% for 10 minutes.

Operational notes:
- Prefetching/KV-cache warmup: schedule a pre-warm job for 1 hour at 20% traffic to reduce cold-start noise.
- Quantization profile: ship q8_0 artifacts; we'll keep monitored fallback to int8 for long-form generation.

Timeline options (pick one):
- Option A (conservative): Contract signed -> 7 days for infra provisioning -> 3 days staging -> migration weekend in week 3 after sign.
- Option B (accelerated): Contract signed -> 3 days provisioning -> 72h staging -> migration weekend in week 2 after sign (requires expedited provisioning SLA).

Attachments: redwood-sizing-v1.xlsx (workbook), SLA-notes.md (short).

Happy to present this on Monday call.

— Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer
